observation.visible_scene: A coastal dusk/sunset landscape. The left foreground holds a large leaning tree trunk and several silhouetted trees on a grassy slope. Most of the frame is open sea stretching to a flat horizon, above which a heavily clouded sky shows a band of golden-orange glow near the horizon. A tiny dark speck (likely a buoy or distant vessel) sits on the water near the center, and a faint landform is visible on the horizon left of center.
visible_changes: The cloud masses drift and morph continuously across the sky: the dark cloud bank at top-center changes shape and extent, and the right-edge cloud bank reshapes, while the bright sunset band near the horizon persists but varies in width and position of its edges.
The sea surface texture and the pale reflection column in the center-right water shift subtly frame to frame, indicating moving water/ripples rather than a frozen surface.
The foreground tree trunk, silhouetted trees, grassy slope, horizon line, and the distant landform remain in fixed positions throughout, indicating a static camera with no pan, tilt, or zoom.
The small dark speck on the water stays near the same location with at most a very slight positional change.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the clouds keep drifting, the glow fades to night, or the scene brightens after the excerpt ends.
The state of the sky and water before the first frame.
The true identity and motion of the small speck on the water.
uncertain_details: The exact direction and speed of cloud drift (gradual horizontal movement vs. in-place morphing is hard to separate).
Whether water-surface changes are waves, current, or shifting reflections.
Whether the tiny water speck moves at all or is a stationary marker.
